names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 11 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Ιωσήφ ο Ιερομάρτυρας», with the rank words left off. No Russian form is recorded: saint.gr prints none.

birth.note: saint.gr: «γεννήθηκε στο Αστραχάν το 1579 μ.Χ.», and the head line of the same page gives «(1579 - 1672)».

death.note: saint.gr: «Στις 11 Μαΐου του 1672 μ.Χ. και κατά την διάρκεια μια επαναστάσεως των κατοίκων της πόλεως, ο Άγιος Ιωσήφ τελειώθηκε μαρτυρικά», and the head line of the same page gives «(1579 - 1672)». The day of his death is the day the calendar keeps him.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026). He is a Russian saint, canonised by the Russian Synod in April 1918 according to this page, and that calendar is the one that would settle his own day; it was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 11ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Ιωσήφ ο Ιερομάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 11 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and the day is the day of his death. **The day's line gives him no see and the life page does**, «πρώτος Μητροπολίτης Αστραχάν», first Metropolitan of Astrakhan, which is why the display name and `office` carry it and the stored Greek form does not. **He is none of the Josephs the name sweep raised**, all of them on the fold of the name, and he is not `joseph-of-optina`, whose Greek row comes off 9 Μαΐου two days earlier in this same wave. **The eyewitnesses are named on the page and are not `related` rows**: his martyrdom was recorded in detail by two eyewitnesses, priests of the cathedral of Astrakhan, Fr Cyril and Fr Peter, who have no folders in this corpus. **The page does not say how he was killed** — only «τελειώθηκε μαρτυρικά» during a rising of the townspeople — and nothing is supplied here. **`locations` are left out**: Astrakhan is his birthplace, his monastery, his see and his resting place all at once, and the page locates it no further. No hymn.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
